title: Week Ahead — Week of Nov 2, 2026 (Sunday-night update)
html:
Sunday night bought the dip. Monday has to prove it.

Futures opened higher tonight, led by the same AI chips that got hammered last week. That's encouraging, but a quiet overnight bounce isn't a verdict. This week brings Apple, Palantir, AMD, Airbnb, the midterms and a jobs report.

The one thing

SPY's floor is $752, then $743–745. Its ceiling is $763.50–767. Tonight's bounce lands in the middle, so nothing is decided yet.

SPY closed Friday at $755.72 (−1.8%). Overnight it trades near $759.66 (+0.5%). S&P futures +0.4%, Nasdaq futures +0.9%. WTI −3% to about $101 after OPEC+ held output steady. A close above $763.50 = buyers back. A close below $743 = defense.

The week

  • Mon: Apple and Palantir report after the close.
  • Tue (big day): Midterm elections; AMD and Super Micro earnings.
  • Wed: Election reaction, ISM services; Qualcomm and Arm after the close.
  • Thu: Airbnb after the close; two Fed speakers.
  • Fri (big day): October jobs report, 8:30 a.m. Fed at 3.75–4.00%; ~80% odds of a December hike. September added only 29,000 jobs.
  • Next FOMC Dec 8–9. NVDA reports Nov 17, DELL Nov 24. See Fed Tracker and Federal Reserve.

Themes

  • Oil shock / Iran (XOM, XLE, USO): winning, cooling tonight. Hormuz still effectively shut.
  • Travel & hotels (HLT, RCL, DAL): winning; cheaper oil helps. BA the exception.
  • Defense (LMT): near highs, RSI 76 overbought.
  • Defensive rotation (KO): staples up while tech fell; 9 of 11 sectors rose last week.
  • Rates & the Fed (TLT, IWM): undecided until Friday.
  • Mega-cap tech (AAPL, AMZN, GOOGL): split; AAPL +27% YTD, GOOGL broke down.
  • AI chips (NVDA, AMD, MU, SMH): losing (~$5T off since Oct 6), bouncing 2–3% overnight on their 200-days.
  • AI vs software (NOW, PLTR): losing badly.

Your names

  • HLT — Ready on trigger. Buy a dip toward $349 (23.6%) or a close above $364.50. Out on a close below $335.
  • DAL — Watch oil. Pressing the 50% level at $80.24. Trigger: close above $80.25. Back off below $79.49.
  • BA — Wait for the bounce. Put after a failed rally near $183–185 or a close under $165.
  • PLTR — Avoid until after earnings (Mon). Then watch $186.90 (50-day) vs $172.23 (38.2%).

Lesson: an overnight move is a hint, not a verdict

SPY traded 77.7M shares in Friday's regular session; tonight's overnight session, about 70K (~0.1%). Thin volume lets a few orders move price. Let the regular-session close decide — that's why every trigger says "a close above/below."

Plays to study (Options Playbook)

  1. HLT Dec 18 $380 call ≈ $515, delta 0.27. Enter on dip to $349 or close > $364.50. Exit close < $335.
  2. NVDA Dec 18 $220 call ≈ $648, delta 0.35. Enter on close > $210. Exit close < $200. Out before Nov 17 earnings.
  3. DAL Dec 18 $80 call ≈ $505, delta 0.56. Enter close > $80.25. Exit close < $79.49 or oil spike.
  4. BA Dec 18 $170 put ≈ $670, delta 0.43. Enter after failed rally near $183–185. Exit close > $196.

Costs = Webull mids at Friday's close; verify live in Webull.

Skip: holding through earnings (AAPL, PLTR, AMD, SMCI, ABNB); chasing the overnight chip bounce before a close confirms; delta < 0.20 lottery tickets; dip-buying DELL.

Homework

  1. Draw $763.50, $752 and $743 on your SPY chart.
  2. Compare NVDA's 9:30 open with tonight's $207.84.

Question: If SPY gaps up to $760 Monday but closes at $753, what has the day told you, and would you take any of the four plays?
